truths.truth: The stdout test holds the ingest at the testkit fault point AFTER_BLOB and proves the read returned mid-pass from the ready file and no runs row at EOF, with no await_process and no ps poll for a process that may have exited
truths.evidence: Exists/substantive: crates/terminus/tests/hook.rs:738-888. `perl -ne 'print if /^fn reading_the_hooks_stdout_to_eof/../^}/' | grep -c await_process` prints 0; await_process is called only at hook.rs:278 and :1025 (the two sibling tests). The hook command sets fault::AT=fault::AFTER_BLOB and fault::READY at :754-755. The ready file is put in a data dir created first (:749-750). The transcript is now 1 repeat (:745). The runs count is sampled when the poll sees the read result (:809) through a new read-only `runs` helper shaped like `committed` (:917-928). The arrival wait polls only `ready.exists()` with a 20 s deadline (:852-863). The runs_at_eof == 0 assertion comes after it (:867-871). The one ps() call (:875-886) runs after the ready file proves the ingest is in its 30 s stall, then sigkill + drain. Wiring: the AFTER_BLOB stall is in `prepare` at crates/terminus-core/src/ingest/mod.rs:506, before `apply`'s transaction. Every runs insert comes later: record_run inside apply's tx (mod.rs:672-673), pass::record_pass after the walk (pass.rs:508-554), backfill::record_pass (backfill.rs:445-486). spawn::detached passes the env on unchanged (spawn.rs:64-70, spawn_from :118-137). `cargo tree -p terminus -e features -i terminus-core` shows the dev-dependency turning on feature "testkit". Traced value: TERMINUS_FAULT_AT set at hook.rs:754 reaches the detached ingest; fault::stall (mod.rs:897-905) writes the READY path; the test sees it at hook.rs:853. Behaves: the stdout run passed in debug (finished in 0.03s) and --release (0.02s). Passing requires the ready file within 20 s, runs_at_eof == 0, and exactly one held ingest found by ps.

truths.truth: When a process the hook started holds the hook's stdout, the stdout test fails at its 250 ms limit, not after the hold, and names 'a process the hook started held stdout open'
truths.evidence: Observed with no source change. A scratchpad LD_PRELOAD shim made the `hook SessionStart` process fork a child that sleeps 30 s holding the hook's stdout. The test cannot tell this child from an ingest made to inherit stdout. The release test binary panicked at hook.rs:826: "reading the hook's stdout to EOF was still open after 253.1 ms against a limit of 250.0 ms; the hook had exited, first seen 5.1 ms after the read began; the longest gap between polls was 5.1 ms; a /usr/bin/true spawn took 0.3 ms. Verdict: a process the hook started held stdout open". It finished in 0.25s against a 30 s holder, so the read is bounded (reading thread plus a poll loop at :776-807). A control run with the shim loaded but inactive passed. The held branch is the else-if at :818-822. This is the first half of UAT item 3 only. The second half is truth 4.

truths.truth: With the fault point's environment variable removed, the stdout test fails within its 20 s arrival deadline with a message naming testkit, not at CI's 15-minute kill
truths.evidence: Code supports it but no run observed it. With AT unset, fault::stall returns before it writes READY (ingest/mod.rs:897-900), so the ready file never appears. Every step before the arrival wait is bounded: the poll loop breaks at 250 ms (:804-806), and child.wait follows a read that already reached EOF. The arrival wait is bounded at ARRIVAL_TIMEOUT 20 s (:740, :852-863), and its panic text names `testkit` (:856-858). It runs before the runs_at_eof assertion and the ps lookup, so a fast unheld pass cannot fail elsewhere first. Not run: one run lasts the full 20 s arrival deadline, over this verifier's ~10 s per-check limit, and the plan's no-fault mutation edits hook.rs, which this verifier may not do.

truths.truth: A timing miss in either #104 test prints the longest poll gap, a /usr/bin/true spawn time and the hook's own evidence, and names exactly one verdict
truths.evidence: Seven forced misses, all observed on the real limits rather than limit 0 (a missed limit enters the same failure branch), with no source change. Stdout test (panic at hook.rs:826). (a) Shim delays the hook 1 s: 'still open after 252.9 ms ... the hook had not exited; the longest gap between polls was 5.1 ms; a /usr/bin/true spawn took 0.3 ms. Verdict: the hook was blocked'. (b) Same, with the test process SIGSTOPped for 200 ms in its poll window: 'longest gap between polls was 203.3 ms ... Verdict: the runner stalled'. (c) Held stdout: 'Verdict: a process the hook started held stdout open' (truth 3). Stdin test (panic at hook.rs:489; TERMINUS_TEST_DRAIN_DEADLINE_MS is inherited by the hook through Command's default env). (d) 20000 ms: 'still running 10003.0 ms ... longest gap 10.1 ms; spawn took 0.4 ms; the hook had not logged that it stopped waiting on stdin, so it was still waiting on stdin ... Verdict: the hook was blocked'. (e) Same, plus a 6 s SIGSTOP: 'longest gap between polls was 6004.5 ms ... Verdict: the runner stalled'. (f) 100 ms, with an exit-time shim destructor keeping the hook alive: 'the hook had logged that it stopped waiting on stdin, so it was past stdin and had not exited ... its stderr: "terminus: UserPromptSubmit stopped waiting on a stdin that stayed open for 100 ms\n". Verdict: the hook was blocked'. Run (f) exercises the drain-line branch that SUMMARY listed as open. For every captured output, `grep -oE '<verdict phrases>' | sort -u | wc -l` printed 1. Code: one if/else verdict chain per test (stdin :484, stdout :819), sharing runner_stalled (:709-716) and time_a_spawn (:694-705). time_a_spawn runs only on the failure path and goes through `output`, under the COPYING guard. Stall lines are separate values: 5 s (:454) and 125 ms (:770).
